profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point in Porto San Giorgio, on Italy's Adriatic coast, tagged telecom=data_center, is named Studio BETA SRLS. "SRLS" is the Italian legal designation for a simplified limited-liability company, a structure commonly used by small startups, freelancers, and professional practices due to its lower minimum capital requirements, and "Studio" again indicates a professional-services or design practice in Italian usage. As with the similarly named Studio Delta Srl record elsewhere in this dataset, this pattern points to a small office rather than a data-center business. This entry documents the likely mistag rather than fabricating data-center specifications for what is, by its own name, a small professional-services firm.

reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point in Porto San Giorgio, Italy, tagged as a data center, is almost certainly a small professional-services office instead. The name Studio BETA SRLS carries two signals in Italian usage: "Studio" means a practice or office, and "SRLS" is the simplified limited-liability form used by small firms and freelancers. Neither fits a facility that houses servers at scale.

The record reports zero megawatts, no operator, no website, and no specifications. That absence is the point. A genuine data center entry in this dataset would carry power figures and an operator, because those are the facts that matter for compute. Here there is nothing to size, nothing to connect to a grid, and nothing that would add load to the Adriatic coast.

For AI specifically, this matters only as a caution about the underlying map. OpenStreetMap tags are contributed by volunteers and reviewed unevenly, so a tag reading telecom=data_center can attach to a design studio. Anyone counting facilities from this source will overcount, and the error runs in the direction of making distributed compute capacity look larger and more spread out than it is.

What this record does not tell the reader is anything about actual Italian data-center capacity. It is one point, in one city, with no power, no operator, and no verification beyond a tagging review. It documents a likely mistake, not a facility.
